title: Efficacy of probenecid on cluster seizures during dosage reduction of Anti Seizure Medication (ASM) in presurgical focal epilepsy video-EEG monitoring
official: Efficacy of probenecid on cluster seizures during dosage reduction of Anti Seizure Medication (ASM) in presurgical focal epilepsy video-EEG monitoring
summary: Main objective: To assess the efficacy of PBN administration on the cessation of seizure recurrence in patients experiencing a cluster seizure upon discontinuation of ASM for pre-surgical hospital video EEG monitoring.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients between 6 and 50 years old
2. Adults, of any weight, who are free from malnutrition or any condition affecting their physiology to any significant degree; or children and adolescents weighing more than 20 kg.
3. With focal seizures epilepsy
4. Requiring video-EEG recording in Epilepsy Monitoring Units (EMU) for the presurgical evaluation of a focal epilepsy, with planned Anti-Seizure Medication (ASM) withdrawal in order to precipitate seizure occurrence, or without dose reduction in the case of epilepsy whose natural history suggests the appearance of seizures without withdrawal.
5. Able to take an oral therapy
6. Ability to record the patient > 12 hours after the second seizure of the cluster
7. Having received informed information about the study and having signed a consent form to participate in the study. Written consent of both holders of parental authority for minor patients
8. Affiliated or beneficiary to a social security scheme
Exclusion criteria:
1. Hypersensitivity to PBN or to any of the excipients (Microcrystalline cellulose, Hypromellose, Sodium carboxymethylamidon, Colloidal anhydrous silica, Magnesium stearate)
2. Pregnant or breast-feeding woman
3. Known or identified impaired renal function (creatinine clearance < 50 ml/min) in children and adults
4. Lithiasis diathesis
5. Treatment with the following drugs: acetylsalicylic acid and/or methotrexate (Note: the following medications require caution when co-administered: penicillins, quinolones, cephalosporins including cefadroxil, paracetamol, naproxen, indomethacin, ketoprofen, lorazepam, thiopental, olanzapine, famotidine, clofibrate, valaciclovir, aciclovir, ganciclovir, cidofovir, zidovudine, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and dyprophylline)
6. Acute gout attack
7. Hyperuricemia secondary to cancer chemotherapy, radiotherapy or myeloproliferative neoplasia
8. Primary hyperuricemia due to overproduction of uric acid
9. Participation in an interventional clinical study (drug)
10. Patient benefiting from legal protection
